title: A little gift, a familiar shape
say: Have you ever received a present in a box, or maybe in a gift bag? Look at this one. Before we notice the bow, what simple shape can you see underneath?
hint: What shape is hiding beneath the bow?

title: From cube to gift box
say: Remember the cube you drew? This gift box uses the same idea: a top and two sides meeting at corners. But it is stretched into a rectangular prism. Compare their widths and heights. You already know how to begin.
hint: The same three faces · new proportions

title: See the gift, then the drawing
say: Now look more closely. The ribbons cross over the box. There is a soft bow and a little star in the middle. Our teacher begins with the box, then adds those details. Let's enjoy the process.
hint: Box first · ribbons and bow next

title: Keep your drawing tools close
say: Take your sketch paper, a pencil for light guide lines, a softer pencil for shadows, and an eraser. A blending tool is useful if you like a soft finish. Ready? Let's draw together.

title: Pause and point
say: Before the teacher starts, point to the top face, the front face and the side face in the real gift box. Notice which edge is longest. Great. We will build that simple structure first.

title: Find the big shape
say: Watch how the teacher finds the overall width and height. Compare with the real gift box. Keep your first lines light; we can change them. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Check the top and sides
say: The top and side planes tell us where this box sits in space. Follow each edge back and check its angle against the reference. Stop here and compare your three visible faces. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Make room for the ribbon
say: Before adding small details, check the box again. Does the top leave enough room for the crossing ribbon and bow? Make any correction now; changing a line is part of drawing. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Look what you have built
say: You found the big box shape. Nice work! Now we can build it with more confidence.

title: Build the rectangular prism
say: Begin with the box framework, just as you did with the cube. This time, measure the stretched proportions carefully. Try it on your paper before continuing. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Place the lid and ribbon
say: Look for where the lid meets the box, then find the bands crossing its top and front. Let the ribbon follow the box edges instead of floating above them. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Shape the bow and star
say: Now the box can become this particular present. Observe the two bow loops, their overlap, and the little star. Add them after the structure is stable. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Big form first · small details second.

title: Look what you have built
say: Your gift box has its structure and personality. Next, we will make it feel solid with light and shadow.

title: Choose the light and dark faces
say: Remember the cube: each plane catches light differently. Compare the light top with the darker front and side. Keep each value family clear. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Give the ribbon its volume
say: The ribbon bends over edges and around the bow. Shade its folds gently and leave lighter places where the ribbon catches light. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Watch the fold, then the value.

title: Set the box on the table
say: Look for the shadow beneath and beside the box. This contact shadow helps it sit on the surface. Pause and check the light direction before you continue. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Look what you have built
say: Those values give the box real volume. Let us bring the small details into focus.

title: Strengthen the important edges
say: The structure is already there. Now choose a few edges to make clearer. Keep the drawing lively; you do not need to darken every line. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: A few clear edges are enough.

title: Refine the bow and pattern
say: Look at the bow loops, ribbon tails, tiny star and wrapping pattern. Add only what helps this gift box feel like the real object. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: Balance texture and contrast
say: Step back and compare light, middle and dark areas. Refine the paper texture and deepest folds without covering your highlights. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.

title: One final look
say: You made a rectangular prism feel like a present. Check the corners, the ribbon crossing and the shadow beneath. If those read clearly, your core drawing is done. Take your time. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Wonderful work. Your box is complete.

title: Share your gift box
say: You have finished the core drawing. Take a photo when you are ready, and share it for feedback. You can always return to an earlier step.

title: Optional: make it your own
say: If you would like to keep going, add a little background or wrapping pattern of your own. This is optional. Your gift box is already complete.

title: A gift you drew
say: Look what you made! You began with a familiar box shape and turned it into a gift, one careful step at a time. Great work. Ready for your next drawing?
hint: Your Gift Box lesson is complete!
